units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1:16">Y. Peah I, 15ᵇ</cite> bot., a. e. (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 32:47">Deut. XXXII, 47</cite>) <he>ואם הוא ר׳ מכם וכ׳</he> and if it (a word of the Law) appear void (of meaning), it is your fault, because you do not toil to study it.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 4:20">Num. R. s. 4<sup>20</sup></cite> (ref. to <cite ref="II Samuel 6:20">II Sam. VI, 20</cite>) <he>הר׳ שבריקים זה וכ׳</he> the lowest of the low is the dancer, for there is none more void of all merits than he is; a. e.—Pl. <he>רֵיקִים</he>, <he>רֵיקִין</he>, <cite ref="T00693"><he>רֵקִ׳</he></cite>.
Ib.; Y. Succ. V, 55ᶜ top; Y. Snh. II, 20ᵇ bot.; a. e.—[Gen. R. s. 32, end הריקין, read: הרֵיקָן.]—Fem. רֵיקָה.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:3">Num. R. s. 20<sup>21</sup></cite> (ref. to Deut. l. c.) <he>אפי׳ מצוה … ר׳ וקלה בה חיים וכ׳</he> even if there be a command which thou considerest empty and unimportant, there is in it life and length of days.
